name: Tutoring

off_season.play: Sell summer catch-up packages and book fall slots now.

not_yet: Don't hand out flyers at a school without the school's okay.
Don't take on more subjects than you can teach well.
Don't message students directly. Talk to parents.
crowd.note: Safety rules with minors come first: parents book, and sessions happen where a parent can see.
crowd.basis: Scores, buyer, first $1 and not-yet lines: research/crowd.json (our judgment). Best months and the summer dip: research/niches/tutoring.json crowd hint, from its sources.

safety: Parents book and pay. You talk with parents, not students.
Sessions happen where a parent can see: at home with a parent nearby, at a library table, or online with a parent in the house.
No direct messages, texts or social follows with students. Links and reminders go to the parent.
Background checks aren't required for private tutoring in most places, but parents expect one: get one in your own name and offer to share it. Follow any rule your state or a school program has.
Collect contact details from parents only. The FTC's COPPA rule covers collecting information from children under 13 online.

extra.title: Parent call script (15 minutes, free)
lines: 1. Thanks for making time. What made you think about tutoring now?
2. What's the subject, grade and teacher's main feedback? Any test dates coming up?
3. What has your child tried so far, and what helped?
4. Here's how I work: a first session to find the gaps, a plan for 4 weeks, and a short note to you after every session.
5. Safety: you book and pay, sessions happen where you can see, and I only message you, never your child.
6. My founding price is {founding}. Want to pick a first session time?

ai_rules: Write to the parent or the place, never to a student.
Never promise a grade, a score or a result.
Say any price once, exactly as given. The next step is the free 15-minute parent call.

stop.label: Asked you to stop
stop.next: Don't send anything else. They're marked lost so they stay off your lists.

yes.label: They're interested
yes.means: They want to hear more or book.
yes.answer: That's great to hear! The easiest first step is a free 15-minute call: I'll ask about the subject, the grade, any test dates and what times work. When suits you this week?

price.label: They asked the price
price.means: They want the price before anything else.
price.answer: Of course. It's {rate}, {length} one to one, with a short note to you after every session. Want to start with a free 15-minute call to see if it fits?
price.next: Say the price once, then offer the free parent call.

later.label: Not right now
later.answer: No problem at all. Would it help if I checked back before the next test or report card? Either way, my number's here when you need it.
later.next: Set a reminder for 4 to 6 weeks, or just before the next test.

who.label: Who is this?
who.means: They want to know who you are first.
who.answer: Sorry, I should have said! I'm {me}, and I tutor {what} here in {area}. Parents book, sessions happen where a parent can see, and you get a note after every session. Happy to answer any question.
who.next: Answer plainly, then offer the free parent call.

covered.label: They have a tutor
covered.answer: Good to hear you're covered! If you ever need a second option, say for test prep or a summer catch-up, I'm around. Thanks for letting me know.
covered.next: Leave it there. Ask again in late spring if it fits.

question.label: They asked a question
question.answer: Good question! The honest answer depends on where your child is right now, so the best way to answer it properly is a free 15-minute call. Would one day this week work?
question.next: Answer it in a line if you can, then offer the free parent call.

other.label: Not sure what they meant
other.answer: Thanks for getting back to me! Happy to help however I can. Would a free 15-minute call this week be easier to talk it through?
other.next: Keep it short and end with one question.

talk.label: Wants to talk
talk.means: The parent wants to talk first.
talk.answer: Happy to! {when_ask} It's a free 15-minute call: I'll ask about the subject, the grade, any test dates and what times work.

yes.label: They said yes
yes.answer: Thank you, that's great! I'll drop off a few flyers this week. Is there a day that works best, or someone I should ask for?
yes.next: Drop off the flyers within a week and thank them in person.

price.label: They asked the price
price.means: They want to know what families pay.
price.answer: Families pay {rate}, booked and paid by parents, and the first parent call is free. Happy to drop off a flyer with the details.
price.next: Say the price once, then offer the flyer.

later.label: Not right now
later.answer: No problem at all. Could I check back next term? Thanks for considering it.
later.next: Set a reminder for next term.

who.label: Who is this?
who.means: They want to know who you are first.
who.answer: Sorry, I should have said! I'm {me}, a local tutor for {what}. Parents book, sessions happen where a parent can see, and I follow your rules on posting. Happy to come by and say hello.
who.next: Answer plainly, then offer to stop by.

covered.label: They have someone
covered.means: They already work with tutors or a program.
covered.answer: Good to hear your families have help. If you ever keep a list of local tutors for parents, I'd be glad to be on it. Thanks!
covered.next: Ask once about a resource list, then let it go.

question.label: They asked a question
question.answer: Good question! Happy to answer it properly: could I stop by for five minutes, or would a quick call be easier?
question.next: Answer it in a line if you can, then offer to stop by.

other.label: Not sure what they meant
other.answer: Thanks for getting back to me! Happy to work around your rules. What's the best way to share my info with families?
other.next: Keep it short and end with one question.

partner_objections.label: They have rules
partner_objections.means: They have rules about posting or promoting.
partner_objections.answer: Thanks for explaining, and of course I'll follow your rules. Is there another way you share resources with families, like a newsletter or a list of local tutors, that I could apply for?
partner_objections.next: Follow their rules exactly and ask about the approved way in.

objections.label: Can't we use free help?
objections.means: They wonder why they'd pay when free help exists.
objections.answer: Yes, and you should use it! The free practice from school and the College Board is good, and I build the plan around it. What I add is one to one: finding exactly where your child gets stuck, explaining it another way, and a short note to you after every session. Want to try a free 15-minute call?
objections.next: Agree, then offer the free parent call.

sources.says: Free SAT practice resources are available.

objections.label: Can you promise a better grade?
objections.answer: I can't promise a grade or a score, and I'd be careful with anyone who does. What I can promise is the work: a first session that finds the gaps, a plan for the next 4 weeks, and a note to you after every session so you can see what's moving.
objections.next: Never promise a result. Offer the first session and the plan instead.

objections.label: Are you background checked?
objections.means: They want to know their child is safe with you.
objections.answer: Good question, and every parent should ask it. Here's how I keep it safe: you book and pay, sessions happen where you can see (at home with you nearby, at a library table, or online with you in the house), and I only ever message you, never your child. I'll share my background check report before the first session.
objections.next: Send this once your background check report is in hand.
objections.check: Have your background check report ready to share before you send this.

sources.says: Most parents expect a background check when you work with minors.

objections.label: Online or in person?
objections.answer: Either works. Online saves the drive and is often a little lower priced. In person can be at your home with you nearby or at a library table. Which would suit your child best?
objections.next: Let them pick, then book the free parent call.

sources.says: Online tutoring is often slightly lower priced than in-person and offers scheduling flexibility.

objections.label: More than they expected
objections.means: The price feels high to them.
objections.answer: That's fair to ask. Tutoring runs from about $18 to over $100 an hour depending on the subject and grade. For {rate} you get a plan, one-to-one sessions and a note after each one. If weekly is a stretch, every other week works too, or a block of 4 paid up front costs a little less per session.
objections.next: Hold your price. Offer every other week or the block of 4.

sources.says: Rates range from about $18 to over $100 an hour depending on subject, grade level and format.

objections.label: Too busy this term
objections.answer: Totally understand. Two options that fit around a busy week: a short weekly online session, or a focused block before the next big test. When is your child's next test?
objections.next: Offer the smaller step tied to their next test date.

where: At home with a parent nearby

win.prep: Before the first session, could you send me a photo of {for}'s most recent test or homework, and anything the teacher has said? That's all I need to plan. If a test date is coming up, let me know that too.
win.reminder: Hi {greet}, see you {when} for {for_s} session. Nothing to bring except recent homework and a pencil. Reply here if anything changes.

Before: Confirm the day, time and place with the parent in writing.
Agree the rate, the package, when it's paid and the cancellation rule in writing.
Ask for a recent test or homework, and any test dates.
Have your background check report ready to share.
First session: A parent can see or hear the session: at home nearby, at a library table, or in the house for online.
A short look at recent work and a few problems to find the gaps.
Teach one gap, practice it together, then check that it stuck.
Leave 10 to 15 minutes of practice for before next time.
After: Send the parent a short note the same day: what you covered, what to practice, what is next.
Write a simple plan for the next 4 weeks.
Book the next session before you leave or log off.

sources.says: Use assessments to identify student needs, lesson plans and practice materials; for test prep, practice tests are essential.
Establish clear payment terms and cancellation policies upfront to prevent billing disputes.
